introduction.text: The Mitreo delle Pareti Dipinte (III,I,6) was a Mithraeum in Ostia, a Roman city on the coast, notable for its wall paintings depicting Mithraic iconography.

history.description: The Mitreo delle Pareti Dipinte was a Mithraeum located in region III of Ostia, a Roman city on the coast.

design.description: The Mithraeum consisted of a small vestibule leading to a cella measuring 14 by 4 metres, divided by two walls into front and rear sections, each with benches for initiates. The rear floor was decorated with travertine, the front with a stepped marble altar built in opus vittatum.

art.description: Wall paintings include figures of Mithra (Sol-Mithras) with a bust, the lunar symbols, the attendants Cautes and Cautopates, a figure with a cloak, a figure with a javelin, and Venus.
